newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Harvey Nichols profits up 35 percent.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Harvey Nichols profits up 35 percent.

text.p: High class fashion store Harvey Nichols, often described as Princess Diana's favourite shop, on Thursday displayed a 35 percent rise in first half profits and said its top designer labels were still very much in demand.

Pretax profits from the retailer, which made its stock market debut earlier this year, rose to 5.5 million pounds ($9.08 million) from 4.09 million in the half year to September 28. Sales rose 16 percent to 49.18 million pounds from 42.38 million. The interim dividend was 1.9 pence a share.

The group, controlled by Hong Kong-based Dickson Concepts, said sales in its flagship store in London's exclusive Knightsbridge district were up 16 percent in the first nine weeks of its current half year.
The shares, which have stormed ahead since flotation, stood eight pence higher at 352.5 pence. They were floated in April at 270 pence.
The group opened a stand-alone restaurant, The Oxo Tower, on the south bank of the Thames in September and opened its first store outside London in October in the northern city of Leeds.
Chairman Dickson Poon said in a statement, "The Oxo Tower restaurant brasserie and bar, and the Leeds store have been performing better than anticipated."
Finance director Clive Morton was optimistic about prospects for the second half. "We expect strong trading to continue," he told Reuters in an interview.
He attributed the store's success to management's ability, buying the right stock and creating the right ambience for its wealthly fashion-loving clientele.

The company is looking to open two more regional shops, one in Manchester in the northwest of England and one in Glasgow. Morton said the group was looking for sites, but had nothing to announce at this stage. He said there were a couple of sites under consideration in London for expanding the company's restaurant business.

The group spent 5.5 million pounds in the first half on its Knightsbridge store and the development of the Oxo Tower. Morton said in the second half the group would make a nine million pound payment related to the new Leeds store opening, plus a further two million pounds on a 4,000 square foot extension of the menswear department at Knightsbridge.

The store, founded by Benjamin Harvey in 1813, started out selling oriental rugs and silks. It became part of the Debenhams department store chain in 1919 and was sold to Dickson Concepts in 1991 by Burton, the owner of Debenhams.
